tasks.title: Read: Hi, I'm Good Old Earth

passage.title: Hi, I'm Good Old Earth
passage.text: Hi, kids! It's me, Earth. You can call me Good Old Earth. From space, I look mostly blue, because I am covered with lots of water. The green and brown parts are land. A blanket of air is all around me. People, animals, and plants all share the land. Trees and flowers give homes and food to birds, bees, and squirrels. Rivers, lakes, and oceans are homes for fish and turtles. I am glad you are here with me. Please help take care of me!

passage.title: Garbage
passage.text: Hi, it's Earth again. Let's talk about trash. Trash is stuff you used and do not need anymore. After a party, you put paper plates, napkins, and plastic spoons in the trash can. When the trash bag is full, someone takes it outside. A garbage truck comes once a week and takes the trash away. It takes the trash to a landfill. A landfill is a big place where trash is buried in the ground. There is a lot of trash on me!

passage.title: Natural Resources
passage.text: Earth here! Natural resources are things that come from nature. People do not make them. Water and trees are two natural resources. You drink water. You use water to take a bath, wash dishes, and grow food in a garden. Trees give us wood to make houses, tables, and pencils. Paper is made from trees, too! Trees also help clean the air. Some places, like a desert, have very little water. It is hard to live there. Please do not waste natural resources!

passage.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
passage.text: People make lots of trash, but you can help! Remember three words: reduce, reuse, and recycle. Reduce means to use less. Use just one paper towel, not five. Reuse means to use something again. Draw a picture on the back of old paper. Recycle means to turn old things into new things. Put paper, cans, glass, and plastic bottles in a recycling bin. A truck takes them to a recycling center. Old plastic bottles can become new toys!

passage.title: Composting
passage.text: Meet the Smith family. After dinner, there are food scraps that no one can eat, like carrot peels and lettuce leaves. The Smiths do not throw them in the trash. They put them in a compost pile in the backyard. Worms and tiny living things help the scraps rot. After a while, the scraps turn into dark, rich soil called compost. The Smiths put the compost in their garden. It helps the vegetables grow big and healthy! Composting is a kind of recycling.

passage.title: Pollution
passage.text: Look at these two beaches. One is clean. One has trash all over it. Trash that is left on the ground or in the water is called litter. Litter can hurt animals and plants. Things that make the land, water, or air dirty are called pollution. Smoke from cars and factories can make the air dirty. Dirty air is bad for your lungs. You can help! Do not litter. Walk or ride a bike when you can. Turn off lights you are not using.

lessons.changes: Shortened the story of Willy's trip; kept the leaf, the littered river, the factory, the water treatment plant and why every drop matters; removed fresh-water percentages and factory details; questions rewritten with text evidence; added a retelling task.

passage.title: Willy the Water Drop
passage.text: This is Willy the Water Drop. Willy was resting on a leaf. Then the wind shook the leaf, and Willy fell into a river. The river had litter in it, so Willy got a little dirty. Next, Willy passed a factory. Dirty water from the factory went into the river, too. Yuck! At last, Willy went to a water plant, where people cleaned him. Now Willy is fresh and clean again. Every drop of water is important. Please help keep water clean!

tasks.title: Read: Goodbye from Good Old Earth

passage.title: Goodbye from Good Old Earth
passage.text: This is Good Old Earth saying goodbye for now. Thank you for listening! Remember what you learned. Reduce, reuse, and recycle. Do not litter. If you see litter, ask a grown-up to help you pick it up. Start a compost pile for food scraps. Turn off the water when you brush your teeth. Plant a tree or a garden. If everyone does a few little things, it all adds up to big things! Tell your family and friends to help take care of me, too.
